correctness.rationale: The radical a is the positive root of a^2+(n+1)sa/sqrt(n)+s^2=1, and b^2-a^2=sqrt(n)sa. These identities yield the global containment inequality 1-sqrt(n)sa(|u_1|-1/sqrt(n))^2. For s>0 equality identifies both contact latitudes; s=0 gives the unit ball. At 2n contact vectors derived from a regular simplex, the weighted mean is zero and covariance is identity. Each is a supporting contact with normal parallel to the contact vector. For any competing ellipsoid y+A B_n with A positive definite, the contact inequalities imply tr(A)<=n, so AM–GM gives det(A)<=1; equality forces A=I and y=0, proving unrestricted global optimality and uniqueness. The thin-lens limit follows from the exact slice integral and semiaxis asymptotics. The inspected verifier checks rational identities and finite diagnostics, not the continuum proof.

value.rationale: The all-dimensional exact John ellipsoid, unique global optimizer, offset-independent contact latitude, and nonzero thin-lens volume fraction are natural convex-geometric invariants. These are structural facts not determined by the known lens volume/mean-width formulas or by generic John optimality conditions; they provide a useful benchmark for ellipsoid approximation of a canonical body family.
